chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him saying: 'The people come to be of three types: a scholar, a student, and scum. So we are the scholars, and our Shia are the students, and the rest of the people are scum.'

key_terms.الْعُلَمَاء: The scholars — here referring specifically to the Imams of the Ahlulbayt as the true repositories of knowledge
key_terms.الْمُتَعَلِّمُون: The students/learners — the Shia community who actively seek and receive knowledge from the Imams
key_terms.غُثَاء: Scum, refuse, worthless debris — originally river foam or flood debris; used metaphorically for those of no spiritual or intellectual value
key_terms.يَغْدُو: They come to be/proceed — the verb suggests movement, i.e., that people's state evolves or settles into one of these categories

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the three types of people in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) categorizes humanity into three classes: scholars (represented by the Imams of Ahlulbayt), students of knowledge (represented by the Shia who actively seek to learn), and those who are spiritually worthless scum (those who neither possess nor seek knowledge). This sharp tripartite division was articulated to his followers to motivate serious engagement with religious learning and to emphasize that neutrality or indifference toward 'ilm (knowledge) places a person among the lowest category. The term 'ghuthaa' (غُثَاء) — originally meaning river scum or flood debris — is deliberately provocative, used to illustrate the spiritual danger of ignorance.
